category_specific_evidence: Issue#26848 says things start breaking down around a scale of 100_000 for a feature.
The comment in _ridge.py says using float32 can be numerically unstable for this estimator, so float32 inputs were converted to float64 where the namespace and device allowed.

The removed test code says RidgeGCV is not very numerically stable with float32 and casts input to float64 unless the device and namespace combination does not allow float64 (specifically torch with mps).
The removed test code set tols["rtol"] = 1e-3 for CV estimators with check_array_api_attributes when the maximum-precision float dtype was float32.
PR#33020 states the change removes the need to upcast float32 inputs to float64 because the eigen GCV path is now numerically stable enough to pass the usual tests.

reproduction_risks: The upcast was removed in PR#33020, so a reproduction on the current code path with float32 inputs may not show the old discrepancy.
The 100_000 feature-scale threshold comes from a single issue sentence and is not tied to a specific dtype, alpha, or gcv_mode in the passages.
The torch/mps device cannot use float64, so float32 behaviour there differs from other namespace and device combinations.
